docs.title: NexusFlag CTF API
docs.text: A Python-based, easily-deployable, no-fuss Open Source API for small community CTF (Capture the Flag) cybersecurity events.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Hosting a local Capture the Flag event shouldn't require massive, heavy commercial platforms. NexusFlag is a modern, lightweight API built using FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and SQLite.

Serving as a spiritual successor to BeeCTF, NexusFlag updates the vision of community-driven CTF software for the modern era, emphasizing accessibility, easy deployment, and zero bloatware.

docs.title: Why Choose NexusFlag?
docs.text:
• ⚡ Modern Tech Stack: Powered by FastAPI for incredible speed and automatic interactive documentation.
  • 🐳 Flexible Deployment: Choose between a rapid Docker Compose setup or a native manual installation.
  • 🎯 Focused Architecture: Keeps maintenance simple by acting purely as a robust backend API—bring your own front-end or use the built-in Swagger UI.
  • 🔓 Open Source: Licensed under the GNU AGPL v3.0, ensuring it remains free and open for community-driven events.

docs.title: Quick At-a-Glance
docs.text: Feature Specification Framework FastAPI (Python 3.9+) Database SQLite + SQLAlchemy Default Admin admin / admin123 Interactive Docs /docs (Swagger UI) Front-End API-only (Bring your own front-end)

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text: Ready to spin up your environment? * Head to the Installation Guide for step-by-step instructions on Docker and manual deployment. * Check out the API Reference to explore endpoints, request shapes, and authentication details.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: NexusFlag provides a lightweight RESTful API to manage event challenges, player sessions, and real-time flag submissions.

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text:
All API requests should be directed to your hosted instance base URL:

http://<your-server-ip>:<port>/api/v1

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All protected endpoints require authentication using a Bearer token. You must include the token in the Authorization header of your HTTP requests:

  • Header Name: Authorization
  • Header Value: Bearer

docs.title: Endpoints Summary
docs.text:
Below is a quick reference table of all available API endpoints:

Method Endpoint Description Auth Required POST /auth/login Authenticate player and issue token No GET /challenges Retrieve a list of active challenges Yes GET /challenges/{id} Get specific challenge details Yes POST /challenges/submit Submit a flag for validation Yes GET /scoreboard Retrieve current event rankings No

docs.title: Authenticate Player
docs.text:
Obtain an access token by submitting team/player credentials.

  • URL: /auth/login
  • Method: POST
  • Content-Type: application/json

Request Body:

{
  "username": "cyber_ninja",
  "password": "secure_password123"
}

Response (200 OK):

{
  "access_token": "nf_token_9f8d7c6b5a4321",
  "token_type": "bearer",
  "expires_in": 86400
}

docs.title: List All Challenges
docs.text:
Retrieve all available challenges grouped or listed for the current event.

  • URL: /challenges
  • Method: GET
  • Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>

Response (200 OK):

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "title": "Baby's First RSA",
    "category": "Crypto",
    "points": 100,
    "solved_count": 42
  },
  {
    "id": 2,
    "title": "Hidden in Plain Sight",
    "category": "Steganography",
    "points": 250,
    "solved_count": 12
  }
]

docs.title: Get Challenge Details
docs.text:
Fetch full description, hints, and parameters for a specific challenge.

  • URL: /challenges/{id}
  • Method: GET
  • Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>

Response (200 OK):

{
  "id": 1,
  "title": "Baby's First RSA",
  "category": "Crypto",
  "points": 100,
  "description": "We intercepted this encrypted message using a weak public exponent. Can you decrypt it?",
  "files": [
    "[https://example.com/downloads/rsa_chall.zip](https://example.com/downloads/rsa_chall.zip)"
  ],
  "hints": [
    "Look up small e padding attacks."
  ]
}

docs.title: Submit Flag
docs.text:
Submit a flag attempt for a specific challenge.

  • URL: /challenges/submit
  • Method: POST
  • Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
  • Content-Type: application/json

Request Body:

{
  "challenge_id": 1,
  "flag": "FLAG{rsa_is_easy_when_e_is_small}"
}

Response (200 OK - Correct Flag):

{
  "correct": true,
  "message": "Correct flag! Points awarded.",
  "new_score": 350
}

Response (400 Bad Request - Incorrect Flag):

{
  "correct": false,
  "message": "Incorrect flag. Try again!"
}

docs.title: Get Scoreboard
docs.text:
Retrieve the current public scoreboard rankings.

  • URL: /scoreboard
  • Method: GET
  • Auth Required: No

Response (200 OK):

[
  {
    "rank": 1,
    "team_name": "BitShift",
    "score": 1450,
    "last_solve": "2026-06-06T14:22:10Z"
  },
  {
    "rank": 2,
    "team_name": "NullPointer",
    "score": 1200,
    "last_solve": "2026-06-06T13:10:45Z"
  }
]

docs.title: v1.0.0
docs.text: I am excited to announce the first stable release of NexusFlag, a lightweight, high-performance CTF (Capture The Flag) platform built with FastAPI and SQLAlchemy. This version establishes the core engine for challenge management, real-time scoring, and secure asset distribution.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Dynamic Challenge Engine: Support for multiple categories (Web, Pwn, Forensics, etc.) with configurable point values and difficulty levels.
  • Secure File Distribution: Integrated admin upload system with a secure, authenticated download route for players, preventing unauthorized asset access.
  • Advanced Scoring Logic: First Blood Bonus (automatic 10% point boost for the first player to solve a challenge) and Anti-Replay Guards (built-in logic to prevent double-scoring on solved challenges).
  • Admin Management API: Dedicated endpoints for challenge creation and file management with role-based access control (RBAC).

docs.title: Technical Stack
docs.text:
• Framework: FastAPI (Python 3.12+)
  • Database: SQLAlchemy 2.0 (Modern Declarative Mapping)
  • Testing: Full test suite powered by pytest and factory-boy.
  • Security: JWT-based authentication and secure path-traversal protection for file handling.

docs.title: Installation Guide
docs.text: NexusFlag supports two primary installation methods: a rapid Docker setup or a native manual installation. Choose the method that best fits your environment.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• OS: Linux, macOS, or WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux)
  • Python: 3.9+ (Tested up to 3.14-alpha) for manual installation
  • Tools: pip3, python3-venv
  • Docker Compose: Required if you choose the Docker installation method (Install Docker Compose)

docs.title: Method 1: Quick Start with Docker (Recommended)
docs.text: The fastest way to get NexusFlag up and running is using Docker. This automatically pulls the environment, installs dependencies, and seeds your initial database.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jremes-foss/NexusFlag.git
cd NexusFlag

docs.title: Launch with Docker Compose
docs.text:
docker-compose up --build

Once running, the API will be available with the following specifications:

  • API Base: http://localhost:8000
  • Interactive Documentation (Swagger): http://localhost:8000/docs
  • Default Admin Credentials: admin / admin123

docs.title: Useful Docker Commands
docs.text:
View logs for debugging

docker-compose logs -f

Stop the services

docker-compose down

docs.title: Method 2: Manual Installation
docs.text: If you prefer to run NexusFlag in a native environment, follow these steps.

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/jremes-foss/NexusFlag.git
cd NexusFlag

docs.title: Set Up Virtual Environment
docs.text:
python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Install Dependencies
docs.text: pip install -r requirements.txt

docs.title: Initialise and Seed the Database
docs.text:
export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:.
python3 seed.py

docs.title: Running API Manually
docs.text:
Once installed and seeded, run the API using Uvicorn with auto-reload enabled:

uvicorn app.main:app --reload

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Database schema changes: If you modify the database models, delete the nexus_flag.db file and re-run python3 seed.py to apply your changes cleanly.
